title: WPSS/1539/2020 of VIBHOR Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
SL.
No Date

COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
WPSS No.1539 of 2020
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Shikhar Kacker, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mrs. Anjali Bhargawa, Addl. C.S.C. for the
State of Uttarakhand.
The brief facts of the case are, that the
petitioner who was serving with the respondents as
a contractual employee at the relevant point of time
was posted in Block Chakrata as a Junior Engineer
and was working on contractual basis. In relation to
the certain projects, which were being undertaken
under the MGNREGA Scheme for the period from
2010-2011 till 2014-2015, certain discrepancies in
the execution of the project was said to have been
highlighted, at the later stage and as a consequence
thereto the services of the petitioner were dispensed
with, with an observation made therein in the
impugned order, that the petitioner was found to be
instrumental in misappropriation of the public
exchequer, as well as, an allegation of certain
professional irregularities, was also levelled against
him by the impugned order of dispensation of his
services dated 21.10.2020 & 14.09.2020. There
would be two arguments to be dealt with.
1. The admitted position, which has emerged is
that the petitioner was contractually appointed at
that relevant point of time, when the set of
allegations were said to have been found to be
levelled against him, constituting as to be the basis
for passing the impugned order, the issue would be
as to whether in the capacity of being a contractual
employee, the petitioner, was at all entitled for
being given an opportunity of hearing or the
proceedings was required to be dealt as per Rule 7
of the Uttarakhand Government Servant (Discipline
and Appeal) Rules, 2003.
Though, principally had it been a simplicitor
order of termination, the necessity of compliance of

Rule 7, qua the services of the contractual employee
would not have been necessitated at all.
But, in the instant case, if the impugned order
is taken into consideration, where the stigma is
being attached in relation to the conduct of the
petitioner, while passing the impugned order, this
Court is of the view, that when a stigmatic order is
being passed, as against even a contractual and
temporary employee, there has had to be an
adherence of the principles of natural justice and a
rational proceedings has to be conducted by the
respondents, before dispensing the services because
any stigmatic order of dismissal/removal of an
employee from the services would in future debar
him from his other public employment avenues.
Apparently, the order does not speak, that
any opportunity of hearing or the proceedings under
Rule 7, was ever conducted by the respondents for
removing the petitioner on the basis of the set of
allegations observed in the impugned order of
21.10.2020 & 14.09.2020.
On this short precise note, that since it is a
stigmatic order of dismissal from services, though
on contractual basis, respondents were supposed to
adhere to the principles of natural justice and they
ought to have conducted an inquiry, as it has been
laid down by the Division Bench of Jharkhand High
Court in Pintu Kumar Yadav vs. Director
General of Police and others in WPSS No.398 of
2015 that even a temporary or contractual
employee, whose services has been dispensed with
on the basis of an appreciation of his service
conduct, has had to be provided with an opportunity
to defend himself.
Consequently, the writ petition is allowed.
The impugned order of 21.10.2020 & 14.09.2020 is
hereby quashed. The allowing of the writ petition
will not create an embargo, as against the
petitioner's employer to reinitiate the proceedings
of enquiry with regards to the conduct of the
petitioner and then take an appropriate decision
after complying with the provisions of Rule 7 of the
Rules of 2003.
This judgment would read only qua the
petitioners whose involvement is reflected from the

order passed by the District Magistrate and will not
govern other employees who are covered by the
impugned order of the District Magistrate.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.) 14.12.2021
